name: Voice assistants
title: Why early voice assistants failed, and when they became viable
question: Why did early voice assistants fail, and when did they become viable?
answer: Wildfire Communications (1992) sold a speech-based electronic secretary from 1994 that answered calls and took voice commands; Orange bought it for $142M in 2000 and ended the product in 2005 for lack of use. Speech recognition before deep learning made too many errors for open-ended requests. Deep neural networks cut recognition errors sharply from 2012, and Siri (2011) and Alexa (2014) followed.
verdict_reason: Deep-learning speech recognition (2012) made open-ended voice commands usable.

constraint.name: Speech recognition accuracy
constraint.detail: A voice assistant fails if it mishears a large share of requests; pre-2012 recognisers did.

crossing.text: Deep neural networks adopted for speech recognition in production systems.
